note: Majority: the National Civil (Code) Act, 2017 (2074), Act No. 34 of 2017, s. 2(e): a minor is a child who hasn't attained eighteen; the Act sets no separate age of majority, so the form holds eighteen from it. Read 2026-11-03 in FAOLEX's copy of the English text, which doesn't say it is the Law Commission's (whose act indexes load by script and gave no link on 2026-10-31). The marriage age (twenty) is another rule and isn't held. Work: the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 2056 (2000), Act No. 1 of 2057 B.S., authenticated 21 June 2000 (FAOLEX's copy of the English text): s. 2(a) a child is a minor not having completed sixteen; s. 3(1) no child under 14 shall be engaged in work as a labourer; s. 3(2) no child in the risky work in its schedule; s. 9 no work from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. and at most six hours a day and 36 a week, which the form doesn't hold. The Labour Act 2074 (2017), Act No. 14 of 2017 (FAOLEX's copy bearing the Law Commission's header), s. 5: no person shall employ a child in any work contrary to law. So general employment from 14, with limits to 16. Whether later amendments changed the Child Labour Act's ages was not read. Performers: neither Act makes an exception for performing, so the form holds barred (my reading of their silence). Service: null. No defence law or ministry page was read (moless.gov.np didn't answer).

sources.title: Child Labor (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 2056 (2000), English text (FAOLEX)
sources.said: "Child" means a minor not having completed the age of sixteen years. ... No child having not attained the age of 14 years shall be engaged in works as a laborer.

sources.title: Labour Act, 2074 (2017), Act No. 14 of 2017, English text (Nepal Law Commission, via FAOLEX)
sources.said: Prohibition on employment of children: No person shall so employ a child in any work as to be contrary to law.
